clue.text: Wild beast and tailless dog getting on

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig

indicators.note: an animal without a tail, so the dog's final letter is docked

parts.note: a dingo is the Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A wild animal and a dog with no tail are setting off somewhere together.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a train or ship means getting on it; the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Old nurse arranged to accept nothing too demanding?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another piece, which sits inside them
the letters of the nurse are put into a new order

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An elderly nurse wonders whether being asked to take on no extra work is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns NURSE into NERUS; 'to accept' puts O inside it to give NEROUS, after O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous duties are burdensome, placing excessive demands on whoever bears them.

clue.text: Sorry company's competitor has lost heart

parts.note: rep is short for repertory company, a theatre troupe

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed, as if its core were gone

parts.note: an entrant is someone who enters a contest

explanation.surface: A firm regrets that a rival has become discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost heart' removes R, the central letter of ENTRANT, leaving ENTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for a wrongdoing is penitent, feeling remorse — the adjective matches exactly.

clue.text: Film company popular before decline

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
to die away is to fade or decline

explanation.surface: A movie studio enjoyed success before falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: An indie is an independent production firm, especially for films or records, outside the big studios.

clue.text: Environmentalist added to graph on recycling: that's the spirit

parts.note: a Green is a supporter of environmental politics
a chart is a graph or diagram
recycling something is putting it to use again

explanation.surface: An ecologist is adding something to a recycling graph, cheered on with an encouraging phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's the spirit' sounds like cheering, but it is the definition: Chartreuse is a French liqueur, a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Chartreuse is a strong herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so it is literally a spirit.

clue.text: Boy ran amok in noble land

indicators.note: running amok is going wild, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lad went wild in the grounds of an aristocrat's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A barony is the domain or rank held by a baron, a nobleman's territory.

clue.text: A holiday with a dog, proceeding northwards round lake somewhere in Ukraine

indicators.note: the turned letters go round another piece, which ends up inside them
in a down entry, going north means reading from bottom to top, so the assembled string is turned around

parts.note: vac is short for vacation
lab is short for Labrador
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A traveller on vacation with a dog heads north around a lake somewhere in Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeding northwards' turns AVACALAB into BALACAVA; 'round' then puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaclava is a town in Crimea, scene of the Charge of the Light Brigade, a place in Ukraine.

clue.text: Oddly nude, streak about, being so lustful?

indicators.note: the first piece goes about the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a ray is a streak or beam of light

indicators.note: takes the first and third letters of the word, the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A naked runner streaking about is asked whether that makes him feel amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streak' paints a naked dash across a pitch, but here it is only a beam of light; 'Oddly' and 'about' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is informal British for sexually aroused, a synonym of lustful.

clue.text: Very tearful female relative accepts one award

indicators.note: the relative takes in the other pieces, which sit inside her

parts.note: nan is a grandmother
I is the Roman numeral for one
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A grandmother cries her eyes out on receiving an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children, so the adjective describes extreme weeping.

clue.text: What about vinyl record, one by the Beatles?

indicators.note: turned about, so the interjection is read backwards

parts.note: eh is a questioning 'what?'
an LP is a long-playing vinyl album

explanation.surface: Someone queries an old vinyl LP, asking whether it is one of the Beatles' records.
explanation.definitionFit: Help! is a 1965 Beatles album and song, so it is one record by the band.

clue.text: Thinking about duke — one fighting at Waterloo with no end of spirit

indicators.note: the named letter is left out of the general's title

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington commanded at Waterloo in 1815

indicators.note: the final letter of the word spirit

explanation.surface: Musing about a duke who fought at Waterloo but whose spirits had flagged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of spirit' is T; 'with no' removes it from WELLINGTON, giving WELLINGON.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on a subject is to brood or keep pondering it, a phrasal verb for thinking about it.

clue.text: 007 embraces new nice lady, corrupted before end of the film

indicators.note: the spy wraps around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: James Bond's code number is 007

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled, so these letters are mangled into a new order
the last letter of the word 'the'

explanation.surface: James Bond clinches a pretty woman who has gone bad before the movie closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of the film' looks like one phrase; 'end of' takes only from 'the', and 'film' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie and Clyde is the 1967 Arthur Penn movie about the Depression-era outlaw couple.

clue.text: Not standing upright, like worker after end of toil

indicators.note: the insect is placed after the preceding letter

parts.note: as means like, in the way of

indicators.note: the final letter of the word toil

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer slumps at the end of a hard day's toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slope or angle, so not vertical.

clue.text: Many in south condemned female writer

indicators.note: the writer's name goes into the rearranged letters
condemned suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.surface: A great many people in the south have denounced a woman author.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order hides the container: the writer goes in the rearranged direction word. George Sand was a nineteenth-century French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means a great number, a large indefinite quantity just as many does.

clue.text: Savages ambassador close to capital city

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: An envoy posted near a capital city lays into its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savages' looks like a verb, as in attacks fiercely; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, heathens were uncivilised unbelievers, a dismissive synonym for barbarians.

clue.text: Dull journalist's wish overturned by editor

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned over means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A reporter's request gets thrown out by the newspaper's editor as boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed phrases are stale and overused, lacking freshness — boringly unoriginal.

clue.text: Devon's equivalent to Rushmore, might one say?

definitions.text: Devon's equivalent to Rushmore, might one say?

parts.words: Devon's equivalent to Rushmore, might one say?
parts.note: Mount Rushmore is the famous American landmark; translate its two halves, rush as dart and more as a near-sound of moor, and you reach the upland in the English county of Devon

explanation.surface: Asks which English landmark could be Devon's answer to the American monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush can mean dart, and 'more' is said much like 'moor', so the American name becomes an English one. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor is a wide upland national park in the south-west English county of Devon.

clue.text: In Lincoln you'll see us four inflicting cruelty

indicators.note: these pieces appear inside the president's nickname

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A visitor to Lincoln is told they will find a group of four being cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' could be the English city; here it is the US president, Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive behaviour is cruel and harmful, treating someone violently or insultingly.

clue.text: Approach officers during manoeuvre

indicators.note: the officers come in the middle of the manoeuvre, so sit inside it

parts.note: an act can be a ploy or performance put on to deceive
COs are commanding officers

explanation.surface: Military officers moving closer in the middle of an exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to go up and speak to them, often boldly — to approach them.

clue.text: Support South American fighters at home

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
US means American
the TA, Territorial Army, is the British volunteer reserve
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Backing for South American soldiers when they are back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a weight is to bear or hold it up, a synonym for supporting.

clue.text: Explicit quality of a French book ultimately confiscated by head

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
to book a seat is to reserve it

indicators.note: the final letter of the word confiscated

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Sheerness

explanation.surface: A frank French book ends up seized by the head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confiscated by' looks like a container instruction, but only the last letter D of confiscated is used. A ness is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names openness, the trait of speaking frankly without holding anything back.

clue.text: A party held by sailors: it's a gas

indicators.note: the sailors hold the other letters inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Sailors throw a party and declare it terrific fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a gas' sounds like slang for great fun but means literally a gaseous element.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Hunting dog decapitated bird

indicators.note: having its head cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the beagle is a hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A hound out hunting has beheaded its feathered prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: 'Rheinbund' assembled by German commander in WW1

indicators.note: put together from parts, so these letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Rhine confederation is put together by a German general in the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rheinbund was Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine, a fitting German-looking piece of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul von Hindenburg led German forces in the First World War, later becoming president.

clue.text: Monthly earnings cut for a period of time

indicators.note: a slice cut from the middle of the words gives the letters

explanation.surface: Someone's monthly pay was reduced over a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months make up this span, a standard unit for measuring time.

clue.text: Economist making important points

parts.note: key means crucial or important
N, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: An economist is making some crucial points.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: In conclusion you'll find me doing editor's job

indicators.note: the word me goes inside the conclusion

parts.note: an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: An editor says that at the end you will find them at work on the text.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, which is an editor's task.
